title: Slopes, sums and curves that move

intro.say: Five things a graph can show, each worked out from the formula.

chapters.title: From a secant to a tangent
chapters.say: What is the slope of a curve at a single point?

beats.say: Take the parabola, and draw the line through its points at x equals 1 and x equals 3.
That line is a secant, and its slope is {slope}.
Now slide the second point toward the first. The slope settles on {slope}: the slope of the tangent.

chapters.title: From rectangles to an area
chapters.say: And how much room is there under a curve?

beats.say: Four rectangles under the parabola, from 0 to 2, add up to {sum}.
Eight give {a.sum}, sixteen give {b.sum}, and sixty-four give {c.sum}.
The sums close in on the area itself, which is about {area}.

chapters.title: Places worth finding
chapters.say: The engine can look for the interesting points itself.

beats.say: This cubic has a peak at x equals {top.x}, where it reaches {top.y}.
Add the line y equals x. The two meet at {m.x}, {m.y}.
And between zero and that crossing, the area between them is {area}.

chapters.title: Curves that move
chapters.say: Some ideas are about how a curve changes.

scenes.heading: One more term at a time

beats.say: Here is the sine, and the straight line that copies it at zero.
Add the cubic term, then the fifth power, then the seventh.
Each term lets the copy follow the wave a little further.
Or let a number in the formula run. Here k goes from 1 to 4, and the wave tightens as it does.

chapters.title: Angles and edges
chapters.say: Two last shapes: a curve drawn by angle, and a curve with limits it never reaches.

beats.say: Here the distance from the origin depends on the angle, and the curve is a cardioid.
At a quarter turn it is one unit up, and heading down to the left.
This curve shoots off beside x equals 1, and flattens toward zero far to either side.
The engine checks both claims before it draws the dashed lines.
